A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of a continuously excited YAL:Nd3+ master laser allows one to obtain a train of picosecond pulses at the output of the OPO, the duration of which is limited only by the duration of the pump radiation pulses.
the use of the YAG:Nd 3+ laser as the source for the parametric generator is a very effective method of obtaining short optical pulses in the infrared region.

the optical parametric oscillator (OPO) pumped by the radiation from a continuously exciting YAG:Nd ^{3+} laser has a number of important advantages over the OPO pumped by the radiation of the conventional Q-switched lasers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a picosecond OPO pumped by radiation from an actively mode-locked laser can operate in a continuous mode.
a picosecond optical parametrical oscillator pumped by a YAG:Nr3+ laser can be used to generate picosecond pulses of tunable radiation with high efficiency.
the use of a continuously pumped laser as a source of subnanoseond pulses is a promising method for pumping optical parametric oscillators.
